records.c: the panel's characters $80 to $87, the first eight of its own character set, which the video chip reads at $0000-$07FF in bank 0 while it draws the panel, so characters $80 on are these bytes: the running man of the lives ($80-$83) and the wheel icons ($84 full, $85 used)

eight delay counts by the fine vertical scroll (5 or 13 loops), with which irq_panel waits to blank the line above the panel at the same place whatever the scroll; they fill the place of character $88, which the panel never shows

the panel's characters $89 to $E2: the icons of the time, diamonds, grenades, mines and energy lines boxes, small digits 0 to 9 ($A7-$B0), the big digits two characters high (tops $B1-$BA, bottoms $BB-$C4), the frame and its corners ($C5-$DD), and the five fills of an energy cell, empty to full ($DE-$E2)

the damage a weapon does to the levels' tougher enemies, which their routines take off their energy, by the character the hit was drawn with less $D8 ($03E9, set by hit_by_shot): 2 for a shot ($D8-$DC), 99 for the grenade ($DD), 0 for the mine's two characters ($DE, $DF), 20 for the laser ($E0), 1 for each of the whip's characters ($E1-$EE), 20 for the energy lines ($EF, $F0), 0 for the sparks ($F1-$F3) and $D3 for the first debris characters ($F4-$F7); then eight zeros. The table fills the places of panel characters $E4 to $E8, which the panel never shows

the panel as it loads, four rows of 40 character codes: the energy bar, the lives and continues, the time and the four counters in their boxes, and the score; the code writes the numbers over it as they change
the panel's three wheel icons ($84 or $85), drawn by draw_wheels
the panel's energy bar, seven cells of characters $DE (empty) to $E2 (full)
the top halves of the lives counter's two big digits
the top half of the continues' big digit
the top halves of the score's seven big digits
the counters' row of small digits: the time at $07A2, then diamonds, grenades, mines and energy lines ending at $07A8, $07AC, $07B0 and $07B4
the bottom halves of the lives counter's two big digits
the bottom half of the continues' big digit
the time's three small digits
the bottom halves of the score's seven big digits

the colour of each panel character from $98 to $E0, 73 bytes in runs of the colours 9, 10, 15, 1, 14, 13 and 3; panel_colour ($61D8) reads it as $0768 plus the character's code, so its first byte is the colour of character $98
jump table entry the interrupt calls each frame: the hero's movement and collision with the map (hero_move, $0E94)
operand of the jump table's first entry: the address of the hero's movement routine

high byte of the hero-movement entry's operand: death_start saves the pair in $EB/$EC and points it at death_animation, the end of a death points it at $08xx or $60xx, and $5736 puts the saved routine back; a level can point it at its own routine (level 1-1 at $AA0D)
jump table entry the interrupt calls each frame: decides which way the screen scrolls next; the start-up writes its operand (scroll_decide, $1261)
operand of the scroll-decision entry, written by the start-up at $55EF ($1261)
high byte of the scroll-decision entry's operand, written by the start-up at $55F6
jump table entry for the level's object routines: tests the screen under the object in X for one of the hero's shots, which are drawn as characters $D8 and up; carry set on a hit ($5FB0)
jump table entry for the level's object routines when an object touches the hero: takes energy off the panel's bar ($3FB5)
jump table entry for the level's object routines: adds the points the caller put, one decimal digit to a byte, in $020F-$0215 (most often 1 in $0213, a hundred) to the score ($3E22)
every object routine ends with a jump here: the LDX's operand at $0859 holds the slot number the routine stored on entry, so the object loop at $0CE4 carries on with the next slot
operand of the LDX at $0858: each object routine stores its slot number here (STX $0859) on entry
a lone RTS, the target of the stub at $0864 and of the level hook at $AE0B
jump table entry for the level's object routines: frees the object's slot ($5F9F)
jump table entry: the level's own code for a frame when the level runs its own sprites ($03ED set), at $FCE2 in the level file
called by the bottom interrupt while paused in a level that runs its own sprites; jumps to the RTS at $085D
three more jump table entries: $27F2, $2885 and $2856, the routines that draw a new row or column of map blocks into the hidden screen
the hero sprite's first colour (red), put in sprites 0 and 1 when standing
the hero sprite's second colour (white), sprite 2 standing and sprite 0 as the wheel

five words, $5A9A, $0BF0, $1261, $0E94 and $08D8: the multiplexer's interrupt, the panel's interrupt, scroll_decide, hero_move and the interrupt's exit. The engine itself never reads them; a level's boss reads them to take over the screen and to give it back (level 1-2's at $6C67, $6EA7 and $7141)

low bytes of the eight scroll routines, by direction 1 to 8 (index 0 unused): $1306 up, $1361 down, $13BE left, $143D right, then $14A2, $152E, $15BD and $164F for up-left, down-left, up-right and down-right
high bytes of the eight scroll routines, by direction 1 to 8
low bytes of the eight colour-RAM shift routines, one per direction, which the panel interrupt runs ($1866, $1A49, $1CA6, $1EE9, $2110, $2333, $254A, $2765)
high bytes of the eight colour-RAM shift routines
low bytes of the sixteen screen shift routines: eight directions copying the screen at $C800 to $CC00, then eight copying $CC00 to $C800
high bytes of the sixteen screen shift routines
STX $0859 / JMP $0858, an object routine that does nothing but hand the slot back to the loop

looks for an empty object slot from 10 down to 0; returns with Y the slot and Z set when one is free, N set when none is. The engine never calls it; the levels' own objects do, to start a second sprite or a shot (level 1-2's cannon, flier, platform and guardian among them)
the interrupt's entry, where the RAM vector at $FFFE points: saves A, X and Y, acknowledges the video chip and jumps through $0314 to the handler for this band of the screen
every interrupt handler leaves here: black border, restores Y, X and A, returns from the interrupt
the hand-over from the loader and the restart point after the title: resets the stack, runs the start-up at $5523, then falls into the main loop

the main program does nothing but this: CTRL held pauses the game ($0203), otherwise it jumps to the handler for the game's state ($03F1) through the table at $090A; all the play happens in the interrupts
low byte of the main loop's JMP, written from state_handler_lo
high byte of the main loop's JMP, written from state_handler_hi

low bytes of the six main-loop states: 0 play ($08EA, nothing to do), 1 after a life is lost ($0916), 2 swap the continue screen's characters ($0925), 3 game over ($092B), 4 next level ($096D), 5 load the level again ($09EC)
high bytes of the six main-loop states
state 1: puts the hero back at the last restart point ($5620) and sets the screen up again ($5774, $5746, $566C), then back to state 0

state 2: swaps the 512 bytes at $6301 with the sprite shapes at $E000-$E1FF ($6198), bringing the message sprites (TIME OUT, GAME OVER, CONTINUE) in or putting the level's shapes back, then back to state 0

state 3: blanks the screen, waits for SPACE, loads file CD from the disk and repeats until its marker byte at $BFEF is 1 (side 1 is in the drive), keeps the level's name for the high-score table, loads the title (file 4%) and enters it at $6C03
state 4: counts the level up ($03FC) and loads the next level's file, named in the level's header at $8CA7

blanks the screen, stops the sound, shows the loading screen ($6237/$626B, or $6285 before the ending), loads the file named in $ED/$EE, starts the ending after the thirteenth level, else sets the level up and returns to state 0
sets the state back to 0 (play) and returns to the main loop
state 5, taking a continue: sets the lives to 3 ($FFFD) and loads the level's own file again (named at $8CA5)
waits for the raster to pass line 255, then turns the screen off ($D011 = $04, written through its copy at $D151)
puts the level's sprite shapes back if the message sprites are still swapped in ($03F5)

the interrupt at the top of the play area: switches the video chip to the play screen ($47ED), sets the next interrupt (the multiplexer's, or the panel's at line $D5), then places sprites 3 to 7 for the first five objects in Y order ($BF-$C3) on both screens; runs on into the frame's game logic at $0B48

the first half of the frame's game logic. While paused it does only the hero's sprites; fire unpauses. Counts the level's time down once every 50 frames and shows it on the panel; time up, or the hero off the top or bottom of the map, kills him ($4D6E). Then the hero's movement, sprites, energy lines ($302B) and the scroll decision, and on through the scroll routine's vector at $0718
the paused path: draws the hero's sprites and goes on through the scroll routine's vector at $0718

the interrupt at line $D5, above the panel: waits by a delay from $0440 to steady the timing, blanks the line with an invalid mode ($D011 = $5F), clears the sprites, sets the next interrupt at line $DD, positions the next frame's top sprites ($5B45) and switches the video chip to the panel (bank 0, screen $0400, characters $0000); then runs the colour-RAM shift through $071C

the interrupt at line $DD: shows the panel ($D011 = $1F), sets the next interrupt ($0A15 at line $2A, or $4797 for a level with a split of its own), then with interrupts enabled runs the second half of the frame: new objects from the map ($5923), every object's routine, the weapons, the energy bar's refill, the diamonds collected (50 points each, and a continue for every 300), and the level's own hook at $AE04. While paused it runs none of it, so the objects freeze
low byte of the object loop's JMP, written with the object type's routine from $5BA7
high byte of the object loop's JMP, written from $5BB9
next slot of the object loop, counting down to 0; then the weapon, shot and bonus routines of the frame

draws the hero each frame on sprites 0 to 2 (nothing while $020A hides him). Standing or walking: two multicolour sprites stacked one above the other in the colour at $0870, with a hi-res sprite stretched to double height over both in the colour at $0871, pointers $2C, $2C+1, $2C+2. Rolled up as the wheel: two hi-res sprites at the same place, one over the other, shapes $2C and $2C+1, in the colour at $0871 and light blue ($0DEC). While the shield is on ($BFFD, from the light blue symbol) every other frame shows three sprites cycling through the six shapes listed at $5BA2, in white while the timer at $BFFE is $30 or more, then, as it runs out, in colours picked at random from $5B9E; the timer counts down to the shield's end

moves the hero by the joystick in port 2 and the map under him, once a frame. Finds the screen row and column under the hero ($20-$23), sets his speed ($2B: 1 walking, 2 as the wheel). Up starts a jump on a new press only; down crouches; down with SPACE turns him into the wheel while wheels are left ($03EF); standing still saves his place as the restart point ($DE-$EA). Walls are characters whose entry in the attribute table at $AF10 is positive; a negative entry is something he picks up as he touches it ($3D1F); the attribute $D3 under his feet hurts him ($3FB5)
a byte inside the BNE at $0F0C. The symbol comes from an ORA $0F0D in leftover bytes at $FDED that are not code in this level
the hero in the air: rising through the jump table at $1237 while $26 counts up, or falling 4 lines a frame once it reaches $29; left and right still steer him

up pressed: stops the jump at once ($26 = $21) under a ceiling (a wall character in the three above his head) or near the top of the screen, otherwise starts it. Pressing up as the wheel unrolls him, but only when he faces right and the fine scroll is 3

steps the walking frame every fourth frame through the seven shapes at $1218, faces right, runs the level's walking hook ($AE0B) if it has one, and moves right by the speed unless a wall is in the way (four rows tall, two as the wheel); the wheel bounces off a wall and turns round
the same as hero_walk_right, leftwards, with the seven shapes at $121F
the seven sprite pointers of the walk to the right, used from the last to the first: $52, $4F, $4C, $49, $46, $43, $40 (each shape is three sprites)
the seven sprite pointers of the walk to the left: $67, $64, $61, $5E, $5B, $58, $55
the crouching hero's sprite pointer by facing, left then right: $79, $76
the standing hero's sprite pointer by facing, left then right: $6D, $6A
the jumping hero's sprite pointer by facing, left then right: $73, $70
added to the hero's Y once a frame when he rolls up into the wheel, a small hop: -3, -2, -2, -1, -1, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2 (the eleventh value, 3, is never used, since the count stops at 10)

lines the hero rises each frame of a jump, by $26: 7, 7, 6, 6, 5, 5, 5, then slower down to 0 at step 29, then negative so he falls again; letting go of up jumps to step $21, the first falling step, which is why a short press gives a low jump

once a frame, decides whether the view scrolls and which way. When the fine scroll is at rest ($16 = 3, $17 = 4) it looks at where the hero stands on the screen: left of X $44 or right of $6C scrolls sideways, above Y $50 or below $9C scrolls up or down, both at once diagonally; a jumping hero high on the screen does not scroll the view sideways. It stores the direction (1 to 8) in $19, patches the JMP at $1303 with that direction's routine and marks a scroll under way ($18). With none, it parks the fine scroll and the frame's scroll stage at $2967. It also clears the stage flags ($02BA-$02C1) of every direction but the current one, so a change of direction starts its copy afresh

low byte of the JMP at $1303, written with the chosen direction's scroll routine from scroll_dir_lo; as loaded it holds $FCE2, which nothing reaches, since no scroll is under way before the first is chosen
high byte of the JMP at $1303, from scroll_dir_hi

direction 1, the view moves up the map, 4 lines a frame. Stops at the top of the map ($0B/$0C = 0). The first frame chooses the screen copy for the screen on show ($171A or $17C0); then each frame moves the hero down 4 lines and the fine scroll ($17) on; at each new character row it moves the map row up ($0B/$0C), everything drawn in characters with it (the shots, the laser, the mine, the grenade and the wall debris; $298A), and swaps the screens ($16E0). The scroll stops once the hero is back below Y $70

direction 2, the view moves down the map, 4 lines a frame, until the map's last row ($ADEE/$ADEF). Like scroll_up the other way: copies $18FD or $19A3 and moves the shots with $29E9. At each new character row it stops unless the hero is still in the air ($29), so a falling hero keeps the view following him

direction 3, the view moves left, by the hero's speed ($2B, so twice as fast as the wheel) and twice that in fine scroll ($1A); stops at the map's left edge or once the hero is right of X $48 again. At each new character column it moves the map position left, everything drawn in characters with it ($2A34) and swaps the screens. Pressing up as the wheel at that moment unrolls the hero and halves the speed
direction 4, the view moves right, by the hero's speed; stops at the map's right edge ($ADEC/$ADED) or once the hero is left of X $68 again; moves the shots with $2A93
direction 5, up and left together, 4 lines and 4 fine-scroll pixels a frame; at the map's left edge it becomes plain up, at its top plain left. Moves the shots with $2ADE
direction 6, down and left together; at the left edge it becomes plain down, at the bottom plain left. Moves the shots with $2B65
direction 7, up and right together; at the right edge it becomes plain up, at the top plain right. Moves the shots with $2BD8
direction 8, down and right together; at the right edge plain down, at the bottom plain right. Moves the shots with $2C4B

at each whole character of scroll: queues the colour RAM shift for direction X+1 for the panel's interrupt ($071C), shows the other screen ($0204 bit 4, read by the top interrupt) and points the row tables at it ($0205), and starts the next screen copy for the new screen on show. Sets $0226 so this frame runs the copy's last stage, which draws the new row or column, before the swap is seen

view moving up, screen $C800 on show: copies its rows 6 to 19 one row lower into $CC00 and sets $177D as the stage for the swap frame, which copies rows 0 to 5, draws the new top row from the map ($27F2) and steps the map rows up ($2885)
view moving up, screen $CC00 on show: the same copy into $C800; its swap-frame stage at $1823 draws the new top row

copies the screen row by row from $CC00 to $C800, unrolled. The ending's tune reads this code, from the instruction's second byte at $1808 to $18C6, as its sound program 21 (the ending's table at $B732)

run by the panel's interrupt after a swap, view moving up: moves colour RAM rows 0 to 19 one row down and fills row 0 from the colours $27F2 left at $BFC0, then clears the queue ($071C back to irq_exit) and goes straight on to the top interrupt's code at $0A15
view moving down, $C800 on show: copies rows 1 to 14 one row higher into $CC00; the swap-frame stage at $1960 copies rows 15 to 20, draws the new bottom row and steps the map rows down ($2856)
view moving down, $CC00 on show: the same into $C800, swap-frame stage at $1A06
colour RAM moved one row up for a view moving down, the new bottom row filled from $BFC0

view moving left, $C800 on show: copies each row one column right into $CC00 in three parts, one a frame ($1AE0, $1B1C, $1B5A); as the wheel, which scrolls twice as fast, two parts share a frame. The swap-frame stage at $1B9F draws the new left column from the map ($28BA) and steps the map column left ($293C)
view moving left, $CC00 on show: the same into $C800, its swap-frame stage at $1C82
colour RAM moved one column right for a view moving left; the new left column is filled by the generated code at $CB69, which goes on to the top interrupt
view moving right, $C800 on show: copies each row one column left into $CC00 in three parts; the swap-frame stage at $1DEE draws the new right column and steps the map column right ($2924)
view moving right, $CC00 on show: the same into $C800, swap-frame stage at $1ECB
colour RAM moved one column left for a view moving right; the new right column is filled by the generated code at $CF69
view moving up and left, $C800 on show: copies the screen one row down and one column right into $CC00; the swap-frame stage at $1FE5 draws both the new top row and the new left column
view moving up and left, $CC00 on show: the same into $C800, swap-frame stage at $20B2
colour RAM moved one row down and one column right; the new top row from $BFC1, the new left column by the code at $CB69
view moving down and left, $C800 on show: one row up and one column right into $CC00; swap-frame stage at $220E
view moving down and left, $CC00 on show: into $C800; swap-frame stage at $22DB
colour RAM moved one row up and one column right; the new bottom row from $BFC1, the new left column by the code at $CB69
view moving up and right, $C800 on show: one row down and one column left into $CC00; swap-frame stage at $242B
view moving up and right, $CC00 on show: into $C800; swap-frame stage at $24F2
colour RAM moved one row down and one column left; the new top row from $BFC0, the new right column by the code at $CF69
view moving down and right, $C800 on show: one row up and one column left into $CC00; swap-frame stage at $264C
view moving down and right, $CC00 on show: into $C800; swap-frame stage at $2713
colour RAM moved one row up and one column left; the new bottom row from $BFC0, the new right column by the code at $CF69

draws one row of 40 characters at the screen address in A (low) and X (high) from the map row at $0D/$0E. Each map byte is a block of 4 by 4 characters, 16 bytes in the level's block table, found through $BFA0 (low byte, by the block number's low four bits) and $BFB0 (high byte, by its high four); the row of the block comes from $0225 and the column of the first one from $08. Keeps each character's colour, from the level's table at $AE10, in $BFC0-$BFE7 for the colour shift

moves the map pointers of the screen's top row ($02/$03, row of block $07) and bottom row ($04/$05, row of block $06) one character row down the map, a whole map row (its width, $ADE0/$ADE1) at every fourth
moves the map pointers of the top and bottom rows one character row up the map

draws one column of 21 characters down from the screen address in A and X, from the map at $0D/$0E, column $15 of each block, stepping to the next map row every fourth character; keeps the colours in $BFE8-$BFFC, the bottom row first
moves the map's column ($08, 0 to 3 within a block) one character right, and both row pointers one block right at every fourth
moves the map's column one character left, and both row pointers one block left at every fourth
where each row of a block starts in its 16 bytes, by the row number counted from the bottom: $0C, $08, $04, $00
makes the routine in A and X this frame's scroll stage ($0718), the one the frame logic runs while no swap is due
makes the routine in A and X the stage to run on the frame the screens swap ($071A)

the end of every scroll stage: moves the objects with the scroll ($5A53) unless the game is paused, the level runs its own sprites ($03ED) or one of $017E, $83 (when positive), $0305 or $030D (when negative) is set; then leaves the interrupt

when the view moves up one character, moves everything the weapons and broken walls draw in characters one row down with it: the mine and the grenade ($0305 and $030D, rows $4D and $53), the nine shots ($02F8, rows $3D on), the six debris animations of broken walls ($0334, rows $67 on) and the laser ($036B, row $74); one that reaches row 21 is gone
the view moves down one character: everything drawn in characters (the mine, the grenade, the shots, the wall debris and the laser) moves one row up, and one above row 0 is gone

the view moves left one character: everything drawn in characters moves one column right (the mine's and the grenade's columns $4C and $52, the shots' from $34, the wall debris's from $61 and the laser's $73), and one that reaches column 40 is gone
the view moves right one character: everything drawn in characters moves one column left, and one left of column 0 is gone
the view moves up and left: everything drawn in characters moves one row down and one column right
the view moves down and left: everything drawn in characters moves one row up and one column right
the view moves up and right: everything drawn in characters moves one row down and one column left
the view moves down and right: everything drawn in characters moves one row up and one column left

reads the fire button and F7 each frame, while the hero is on the screen between Y $32 and $B5. A new press of fire jumps to the weapon routine patched into $2D1F (the shot at $3251 or the laser at $3596). Fire held for 35 frames while crouching lays a mine, if one is left on the panel and none is lying: two characters ($DE, $DF) at his feet, whose old contents it keeps at $0301-$0304, with a 50-frame fuse. F7, while no grenade is in flight, throws one ($030D = $D3) from in front of him, if one is left
low byte of the JMP at $2D1F, the routine a new press of fire runs: $3251, the shot, as loaded; the bonus symbols write $3251 for the red symbol and $3596 for the green ($5E39, $5E53)
high byte of the fire routine's JMP at $2D1F

the mine lying ($0305 positive) blinks its two characters every fourth frame by flipping bits in their shapes at $C6F3-$C6FC; when the fuse ($0306) runs out it puts back the characters under it, starts explosions at its place in object slot 1, and shakes the screen for 12 frames ($0305 negative): a random fine scroll each frame ($17, or $16 in a level that runs its own sprites), put back afterwards

moves the grenade ($030D) one column a frame in the direction it was thrown, drawn as character $DD on both screens (on the hidden one at the place the scroll will bring it, $3900/$3909). It explodes when it meets a wall, a character from $D5 up, or an enemy ($1B): a sound, an explosion object in slot 0, 1,000 points, and, except in a boss's level ($03EC) or one that runs its own sprites, every other object on the screen but type 2 explodes with it. The flash that follows is at $2FA9

for 12 frames after a grenade explodes, shakes the screen with a random fine scroll both ways (the hero held steady against the vertical shake) and fades the play area's three colours ($ADF0-$ADF2) from white to black through the tables at $3007 and $3013; then puts the scroll, the colours and the hero's Y back. The third colour ($ADF2) also reads the table at $3013, so the fade written for it at $301F is never used
the grenade flash's first colour, by frame counting down 11 to 0: 1, 1, 15, 15, 12, 12, 12, 11, 11, 11, 0, 0 (white, light grey, grey, dark grey, black), into $ADF0
the grenade flash's second colour by frame: 1 five times, then light grey ($0F) seven times; read for both $ADF1 and $ADF2
a third fade, 1, 1, 1, 15, 15, 12, 12, 12, 11, 11, 11, 11 by frame, which no instruction reads: the flash's third colour reads the second table instead

SPACE fires the energy lines when the hero stands still on the screen (not scrolling, crouching or rolled up) and has one left on the panel: two sounds, $017E = $D3, the save area at $0100-$0129 cleared, then a search down and up the hero's column for the first wall, at most the reach from $324F, which gives the lines' bottom ($5C) and top ($5B) rows. The two lines start at his column ($58) and two to the right ($59). Carry set when they were fired

moves the two energy lines one column apart each frame, the left one left ($58) and the right one right ($59): each line is a column of characters $EF or $F0 in yellow from row $5B to $5C, and the characters and colours it covers are kept in the bottom of the stack page ($012A-$017D) and put back as it moves on. A row of a line stops at a wall or at a character from $D4 up. Each frame the two line shapes ($C778-$C787) are filled with noise, made from the program's own bytes at $08E3 indexed by the timer. Both lines past the screen's edges, $017E goes back to 0
the most rows the energy lines reach up and down: 21 in a normal level, 5 in one that runs its own sprites

the shot, run by a new press of fire: a sound, then a free slot among the nine shots at $02F8 and character $E1 or $E2 by facing, one row below the hero's top (two when crouching) and in front of him. With the red symbol ($3595 = 1 or 2) it fires three shots at once into one of three groups of slots (0 to 2, 3 to 5, 6 to 8) with the shapes and climbs at $3567 and $3570; at the second level every other press uses the wider spread at $3579 and $3582
operand of the CPX at $3312, the loop's last slot, written with the group's first slot minus one ($3298, $32AB, $32BE)

moves each of the nine shots one column a frame, and up or down a row for the spread shots (climb in $02CB: 1 or 4 up, $80 or $84 down, with the shape turned as it bends). A shot is a white character drawn on both screens; it keeps the character and colour under it ($02DD, $02E6). Meeting a wall it becomes a spark ($F1 to $F3, three frames each) and vanishes; a destructible wall character ($3D02) is broken ($3746); a character from $D4 up, which an enemy writes when it is hit ($5FB0), ends the shot at once
the three shots of a red-symbol volley, by slot: characters $E8, $E1, $EC (up, straight, down), repeated for the three groups
the climb of each of the three shots in a volley: 4 (up, turning), 0, $84 (down, turning)
the wider volley of the second red symbol, every other press: characters $E3, $E1, $E5
the wider volley's climb: 1 (up a row a frame), 0, $80 (down a row a frame)
the row each shot of a volley starts on, below the hero's chest: 0, 1, 2
flips between 0 and 1 at each press with the second red symbol, choosing the narrow or the wide volley
the red symbols collected: 0 one shot, 1 three, 2 three with the wide volley every other press. Losing a life takes one away ($564C)
the laser, run by a new press of fire after a green symbol: one at a time ($036B), two sounds, starts in front of the hero, and fills its character's shape ($C701-$C706) with random stripes

the laser is a beam of $76 characters ($E0) that jumps its own length along the row each frame, putting back what it covered (kept at $0341 and $0356). It stops at a wall, breaking up to three destructible wall characters on the way ($3746)

breaks the destructible wall at the screen column in A and row in X: takes a free slot of the six debris animations ($0334), gives 10 points, and writes the level's broken block ($AE00) into the map, so the wall stays gone when it scrolls back into view. It writes the map only when the wall lies at least four characters inside the screen's left, right and top edges and above row 16; nearer the edges the wall is broken on the screen only
operand of the LDA at $3757: break_wall stores the wall's screen column here on entry
operand of the LDA at $3762: break_wall stores the wall's screen row here on entry; a row of 20 or more breaks nothing
operand of the LDY at $378A: the wall's map row (its screen row plus the scroll, in blocks of four), the count of map rows break_wall steps down to reach it

the six debris animations of broken walls: each draws 2 by 2 characters, $F4 to $F7 and then four on every sixth frame up to $FB, on both screens; at the end it draws the level's broken-wall characters ($ADFB-$ADFE) in the colour at $ADFF
operand of the LDA at $38DE: the first of the four character codes of the debris drawn on the screen, which $389D writes before the drawing loop
by scroll direction 0 to 8, the column a cell has on the hidden screen relative to the shown one: 0, 0, 0, +1, -1, +1, +1, -1, -1
by scroll direction 0 to 8, the row a cell has on the hidden screen relative to the shown one: 0, +1, -1, 0, 0, +1, -1, +1, -1
nine bytes 0, 40, 40, 0, 0, 41, 39, 39, 41 by scroll direction, the screen offset of the hidden cell; no instruction reads them

the lightning whip. While the hero stands on the ground and the view is still, holding fire for 20 frames ($85) brings it out, pointing the way he faces ($03C1: 0 right, 16 left, in 32 steps round a circle); left and right on the joystick then swing it round a step a frame. It is drawn from his chest as a line of up to $036F characters, $D8 upwards, whose shapes for the angle are copied into the character set at $C6C0 from the tables at $3C82 and $3CC2, the two sets taking turns each frame, as the colour does. The line stops at a wall and breaks a destructible one ($3B8F). Odd frames put back what the whip covered ($0370, $0398)
low byte of the LDA at $3B6C, written with the whip shape set for the angle ($3C82 or $3CC2)
high byte of the LDA at $3B6C, from $3CA2 or $3CE2
moves the whip's column ($7D) by the angle's column step ($3C22) to the right or left, as $3C02 says
the whip reached a destructible wall: breaks it ($3746) when its top left is on the screen, then ends the whip there
operand of the LDA at $3B98, written with the whip's column (STY $3B99)
by angle 0 to 31, how many characters the whip draws before it steps sideways or up and down: 5 near the horizontal, 1 near the vertical
by angle, how many runs make the whip's line

by angle, which way the line climbs: 0 level (angles 0 and 16), 1 up (1 to 15), $80 down (17 to 31). The table is 32 bytes long and its last 24 are also the first 24 of whip_left_right, which is the same pattern a quarter turn on
by angle, which way the line goes across: 1 right, 0 straight up or down (angles 8 and 24), $80 left; it starts eight bytes into whip_up_down, so the two share 24 bytes
by angle, the columns the line moves across between runs
by angle, the screen offset (40 a row) the line moves up or down between runs
by angle, the rows the line moves up or down between runs
by angle, low bytes of the first set of whip character shapes (16 to 40 bytes, two to five characters)
by angle, high bytes of the first set of whip shapes, $3FF7-$43C6
by angle, low bytes of the second set of whip shapes, drawn on the other frames
by angle, high bytes of the second set of whip shapes, $43C7-$4796
carry set when the character in A is one of the five destructible wall characters at $3D10, with Y its number for the offsets at $3D15 and $3D1A that find the top left of its 2 by 2
the characters of a destructible wall: $CF, $D0, $D1, $D2, $CE
columns back to the wall's top left, by the character's number: 0, 1, 0, 1, 0
rows up to the wall's top left, by the character's number: 0, 0, 1, 1, 0
called when the hero touches a character whose attribute is negative (in A): $80 is a diamond, taken at $3D32; $D3 hurts him, unless he is the wheel or shielded

picks up a diamond (characters $C0 to $C3, 2 by 2) when the vertical scroll is at rest and he is above row 16: a sound, the level's empty characters ($ADFB-$ADFE) drawn over it on both screens, one more diamond counted ($03C7) and the map's block replaced by the level's empty block ($37A0)
columns back to a diamond's top left, by its character $C0 to $C3: 0, 1, 0, 1
screen offset up to a diamond's top left, by its character: 0, 0, 40, 40

by scroll direction 0 to 8, the screen offset from a cell to its place on the hidden screen, used with the row's sign from $3909: 0, 40, 40, 0, 0, 40, 39, 40, 41. Directions 6 and 8 hold 39 and 41, so for a view moving down and sideways the diamond is wiped one column away from where it is on the hidden screen

adds the points in $020F-$0215 (one decimal digit a byte, millions first) to the seven-digit score at $0216-$021C, clears them, and draws the score on the panel in big digits two characters high ($0790, $07B8)
takes one off the two-digit lives counter ($FFFC, $FFFD) and draws it on the panel ($0775, $079D)
adds one to the two-digit lives counter, from the grey 1UP symbol, and draws it
adds the three digits at $02A8-$02AA to panel counter X (0 diamonds, 1 grenades, 2 mines, 3 energy lines), then draws it
draws panel counter X as three small digits (characters $A7 on)
low byte of the LDA at $3EF2, written with counter X's address from $3F29
high byte of the LDA at $3EF2, from $3F2D
takes one from panel counter X; carry clear and nothing taken when it is already 000
low bytes of the four panel counters: $02AB diamonds, $02AE grenades, $02B1 mines, $02B4 energy lines
high bytes of the four panel counters, all $02
where each counter's last digit goes on the panel's row at $0798: $10, $14, $18, $1C
the grenades, mines and energy lines a game starts with, three digits each: 003, 003, 003
draws the wheels left ($03EF, 0 to 3) as three icons on the panel ($074A-$074C), full or empty, with their colours
the last entry of the three icons to draw, by wheels left 0 to 3: 2, 5, 8, 11
four sets of three wheel icons for 0, 1, 2 and 3 wheels left, read backwards: character $84 in yellow is a wheel still to use, $85 in colour 9 one used
the icons' colours, set for set: 7 (yellow) with $84, 9 with $85
draws the continues left, kept in the low four bits of the colour RAM byte $DBEA, as a big digit on the panel ($0778, $07A0)
starts filling the energy bar from empty: all seven cells to $DE and the refill flag $0200 set; the bottom interrupt then fills it a step a frame ($3F98)
one step of the energy bar filling up: the current cell ($0201) goes from $DE to $E2, then the next; the last cell full, the refill ends. While it runs the hero takes no damage
takes one step off the energy bar every other call, unless the bar is refilling or $03F0 is set; at the empty end the hero dies ($4D6E). Recolours the bar by the cell reached ($3FF0)
the colour of the whole energy bar by its last full cell: light red, light red, light grey, light grey, light green, light green, light green

the first set of the whip's character shapes, 976 bytes to $43C6: for each of the 32 angles two to five characters drawn as the line in that direction, with angle 16 sharing angle 0's and 24 sharing 8's
the rest of the first set of whip shapes, from $4000 to $43C6 (the set starts at $3FF7)
the second set of the whip's shapes, 976 bytes, laid out like the first and drawn on the other frames so the whip shimmers

the top interrupt while the curtain runs ($020B): until it has opened, switches the video chip to the play screen, draws the curtain's next step ($4878) and sets the panel's interrupt; once it has ($CB55), it turns all sprites on and hands over to the beam-in ($47D5, $4BD2). Then the level's hook and the sound effects
the top interrupt during the beam-in: video chip set for play, then the interrupt at line $32 that draws the cloud of sparks ($4B77)

sets the video chip for the play area: fine scroll from $16 and $17 (the vertical one through the copy of $D011 at $D3D1), the screen and characters from $0204, bank 3, and the level's three colours $ADF0-$ADF2 into the background and the two shared character colours
covers the screen not on show with the closed curtain: a pattern of characters $D4 $D5 over $D6 $D7, 2 by 2, in colour 9 all over
high byte of the STA at $485D, written with the hidden screen's page plus 3 to reach its last row

one step of the curtain, four 2 by 2 cells a frame from the four paths at $49E7-$4B76, a sound every fourth. Opening ($020C = 0) copies each cell from the screen not on show, with its colours; after 50 steps the bottom row is copied too and the beam-in starts ($CB55). Closing draws the curtain's pattern instead, counting down, and at the end silences the sound and chooses the next state: lose a life (1), game over (3), next level (4) or the continue (5)
high byte of the LDA at $48E5, the bottom row of the screen not on show
high byte of the STA at $48E8, the bottom row of the screen on show
draws one 2 by 2 cell of the curtain at column Y and row A: copied from the hidden screen with colours from $AE10 when opening, the pattern $D4-$D7 in colour 9 when closing
starts the curtain closing: $CB55 cleared, $020C = 1, $020B set, 49 steps to go
the curtain's first path, the columns of 50 cells of 2 by 2: from the middle of the screen it spirals out towards the top left. The four paths together cover all 200 cells of the play area
the second path's columns, spiralling out towards the bottom right
the third path's columns, towards the top right
the fourth path's columns, towards the bottom left
the first path's rows, 0 to 18 in steps of 2
the second path's rows
the third path's rows
the fourth path's rows

draws the beam-in's cloud of sparks with sprite 0 alone: from line $32 it waits for each new raster line and moves the sprite to the next spark's X ($BE15, high bit $BE88), restarting the sprite lower every 21 lines, for 115 lines; then sets the panel's interrupt. Once the hero has appeared ($CB55 = 3) it only places sprite 0 on him

the hero beaming in at the start of a life, in three stages ($CB55). 1: sets up 115 sparks at random X with random speeds, from the program's own bytes ($08E3) as noise, two sounds. 2: for 80 frames moves every spark towards the hero's X, and fills the spark sprite's shape ($FF80) with fresh noise. 3: shows the hero's sprites and fades them in over 16 frames with the colours at $4D5E, clearing the noise a bit at a time through the masks at $CB48; then play starts ($567C)
eight bit masks for the rows of the spark sprite's noise: $F0, $78, $3C, $1E, $0F, $87, $C3, $E1
the colours of the hero's sprites 1 and 2 as he appears, read from the end: black and dark grey flickering, then grey, light grey and white

the hero dies: three explosion sprites set going around him at random delays ($FFD8-$FFF5, in the RAM under the KERNAL), the hero hidden ($020A) and marked dead ($03F0), the movement entry at $0849 pointed at the death animation ($4DBF, the old one kept at $EB/$EC), the weapons taken down a level ($5647) and a life taken ($3E71)

runs instead of the hero's movement while he explodes: the three explosion sprites ($4E21) through eight rounds; then the TIME OUT message if the time ran out, GAME OVER if no lives are left ($6006), or, with lives, the curtain closes ($49D5); a level that runs its own sprites restarts at once

one of the three explosion sprites: waits its random delay, then plays six shapes ($85 to $8A) three frames each with the colours from white through yellow and orange to red, each time at a new random place near the hero, with a sound
the explosion's sprite pointers, read from the end: $85 to $8A
the explosion's colours, read from the end: white, yellow, yellow, light red, orange, red
the offset of each explosion sprite's position registers: 0, 2, 4 (sprites 0 to 2)
masks that clear each explosion sprite's ninth X bit: $FE, $FD, $FB
bits that set each explosion sprite's ninth X bit: 1, 2, 4
the sound voice of each explosion sprite: 0, 7, 14 (offsets into $FFC0)
the sound each explosion sprite starts: $9A, $A4, $8A

the sound effects player, called once a frame: for each of the three voices ($FFC0, $FFC7, $FFCE, seven bytes each) a request with bit 7 set starts that effect; a running effect steps its frequency, waveform and pulse width
silences the sound chip, sets the volume to 15 with the low-pass filter, and clears the effects player's state and the music flag ($0207)

the effects player's loop over the three voices. An effect's program starts with a byte of flags, read bit by bit, saying which of these follow: a jump to another program, attack-decay-sustain-release, a frequency script, a waveform script, a pulse width and its sweep, the filter (voice 1 only), a length; the scripts are then stepped a frame at a time
operand of the LDA at $5074, the filter cutoff, swept each frame by the value at $5078
operand of the ADC at $5077, the filter sweep set by an effect
low bytes of the 41 sound effect programs, by number $80 to $A8 (the first unused)
high bytes of the sound effect programs
the waveform scripts' values for the control register: noise, pulse, sawtooth and triangle, with and without the gate, ring and sync bits

sound effect programs $81 to $99: among them the shot ($82), the whip ($85), the beam-in ($86, $87), the grenade thrown and exploding ($88 to $8A), $8B (rolling up, the whip coming out, a container turning), the continue ($8C), landing ($8E), the energy lines and taking a continue ($8F), a diamond ($90), a broken wall ($91) and the mine laid ($96)
sound effect programs $9A to $A8: among them the explosions ($9A, $9B), the laser ($9D, $9E) and the energy lines' second sound ($A4); the rest are started by the levels' code

prepares a new game: interrupts off, the KERNAL and BASIC banked out ($01 = $35), three continues ($DBEA), clears the game's variables, sets the vectors, silences the sound, builds the colour code ($58B3), draws the panel's counters, sets up the level ($5821) and the stock of weapons, draws the first screen behind the closed curtain, three lives, the laser 5 long and the whip 16, then starts the raster interrupts at $47D5, from which the chain of interrupts runs on
waits for the raster to pass line 255, then turns off the timer interrupts and starts the raster interrupt at line 1

sets the scroll stages to their resting routines, the NMI vector to an RTI ($08E2) so RESTORE does nothing, the IRQ vector to irq_entry, the multiplexer's interrupt, the scroll decision's jump and the hero's movement routine kept at $EB/$EC
sets the grenades, mines and energy lines to three each ($3F35) and draws all four counters; run at the start and after each life lost, so a death gives back three of each
puts the map and the hero back where he last stood still ($DE-$EA), the screen's column offset folded into his X
on a death: one red symbol less, the laser 5 characters shorter (at least 5) and the whip 4 shorter (at least 16)
starts the curtain opening: $020C and $020D cleared, $020B set

sets the hero up for a life: facing right, standing, every flag of the jump, scroll and weapons cleared, the energy bar refilling, the shield off, three wheels ($03EF), the level's time again if it ran out, his position kept on the screen, his sprites' colours, and his movement routine back from $EB/$EC
empties the eleven object slots, parks them below the screen, puts them back in slot order for the multiplexer ($5B89) and sets the sprites' shared colours (light grey and dark grey)
draws the whole play area, 40 by 21 characters, from the map at the restart point into the screen not on show, block by block

the level's starting place from its header: the map position ($ADF3-$ADF6), the rows within the blocks, the map row pointers ($ADE8-$ADEB), the hero's X and Y ($ADF7, $ADF8), saved as the first restart point, and the time ($AE07-$AE09); then the level's own start ($AE01)
clears the game's variables: $0100-$017F, $0200-$0266, $02A8-$030E, $0334-$03CB, and the variables kept in the hidden rows of both screens ($CB48-$CB68, $CF48-$CF68)

writes the two colour-column routines into the hidden bottom rows of the screens, 21 pairs of LDA $BFxx / STA $D8xx each: fill_colour_left at $CB69 for column 0 and fill_colour_right at $CF69 for column 39, and copies the end of colour_shift_up ($18EC) after them
writes the byte in A into both colour-column routines at offset X and moves X on

brings the map's objects to life as the view reaches them. The map is cut into squares of 32 by 32 characters, each with a list of six-byte records (type, state, X and Y in map characters) ending with $D3, found through $8CAA, $8CCF and $8D51 in the level. Each frame it goes through the list of one of the four squares around the view; an object within 44 columns and 23 rows right of and below the view's corner goes into a free slot and its record's type is cleared, so it never comes back
while the view scrolls ($D5 = direction) moves every object by the scroll's step from the tables at $5A8A and $5A92; an object pushed off the screen is removed
objects' X step by scroll direction 1 to 8: 0, 0, then the hero's speed and its negative (written at $5A8C and $5A8D by hero_move), 2, 2, -2, -2
the objects' X step when the view moves left, the hero's speed, written each frame by hero_move
the objects' X step when the view moves right, minus the hero's speed
objects' Y step by scroll direction, from $5A92: 4, -4, 0, 0, 4, -4, 4, -4; its first byte is the last of scroll_step_x

the sprite multiplexer's interrupt: hardware sprites 3 to 7 serve the first five objects from the top; as the beam passes each, this moves it down to the next object in Y order, setting its Y, X, ninth X bit, multicolour bit, colour and shape on both screens, and asks for the next interrupt 21 lines below its old place. Past line $CF it hands over to the panel's interrupt
sorts the eleven slot numbers at $B9-$C3 by their objects' Y once a frame, a selection sort with the highest on the screen last
sets the Y of sprites 3 to 7 for the five objects highest on the screen ($BF-$C3), and the line of the multiplexer's first interrupt ($03EB)
the next hardware sprite's register offset after each: 8, 0, 2, 4, 6
bit masks by sprite 3 to 7, pairs to clear and to set: $F7 $08, $EF $10, $DF $20, $BF $40, $7F $80
the masks that switch a multiplexed sprite on, read at mux_masks + 1 in steps of two
the starting order of the object slots for the sort: 10 down to 0
the frame of each of the three shield sprites, 0 to 5
the frames until each shield sprite's next shape
the shield sprites' Y offsets, by the hero standing or rolled up
the shield sprites' Y offsets when the hero is rolled up as the wheel
the shield's random colours: light blue, white, blue, white
the shield's six sprite shapes: $94, $95, $96, $97, $96, $95
low bytes of the object routines by type: 1 the floating container ($5C14), 2 the bonus symbol ($5D6C), 3 to 17 the level's own enemies through its jump table at $8DD3, 18 the enemy bullet ($5F11)
high bytes of the object routines by type
an object of negative type is exploding: seven shapes ($84 on) four frames each with the colours at $5C0D, a sound at the start, then the slot is freed
the exploding object's colours: white, white, yellow, yellow, light red, orange, red

object type 1, the floating container that holds a bonus: drifts left or right, bobbing on the curve at $5D22 and flashing through the greys at $5D54, and turns back at walls. Shot, it becomes the bonus symbol (type 2) for 500 points. Touching it hurts the hero, unless he is shielded, which destroys it for 100. Its own variables are kept in the hidden rows of the screen at $CC00 ($CF48, $CF53, $CF5E)
the container's bobbing, lines up or down a frame over 50 frames: 0 rising to 4 and back, then 0 falling to -4 and back
the container's colours over 24 frames: black, dark grey, grey, light grey, white and back

object type 2, the bonus symbol, kind 0 to 9 in its state: kinds 0 to 7 float up, the 1UP and the diamond fall to the ground. Touched by the hero it is taken, with 250 points: red the shot's spread (fire runs $3251), green the laser (fire runs $3596, one character longer), blue the whip (two longer), light blue the shield, yellow P a full energy bar, G a grenade, M a mine, L an energy line, 1UP a life, and a diamond
how far a falling symbol drops each frame, read from the end: 0 at first, then 1, 2, 3 and 4
the bonus symbols' sprite pointers by kind 0 to 9: $8C four times (weapons and shield, told apart by colour), $8D P, $8E G, $8F M, $90 L, $8B 1UP, $91 diamond
the bonus symbols' colours by kind: red, green, blue, light blue, yellow, then white
the sound when each kind is taken: $8C for the weapons and shield, $8F or $90 for the others

object type 18, a bullet fired by the level's enemies: flies on its speeds ($CB53, $CB5E), flashing through the colours at $5F6C, and is removed off the screen; it hurts the hero, unless he is the wheel or shielded, which explodes it
the enemy bullet's colours over 12 frames: white, yellow, light red, orange
carry set when the object in X overlaps the hero, with $D6 and $D8 the object's half height and half width
frees the object's slot (type 0, parked below the screen) and returns to the object loop

looks under the object in X at a 2 by 2 square of the screen for one of the hero's shots, which are drawn as characters $D8 and up; on a hit keeps the weapon's number ($03E9, character minus $D8), writes $D4 there so the shot ends, and returns carry set

runs instead of the hero's movement after a death: three sprites stretched to double width drop from the top with TIME OUT ($80 in $03F3), GAME OVER ($81) or CONTINUE with YES and NO ($82), from the pointer sets at $60D6. TIME OUT then goes on to the next life; GAME OVER goes to the continue question while continues are left, else the game ends; the question waits for left or right and fire ($60DF)
three sets of three sprite pointers, read by message number 0 to 2: left $83, $86, $80; middle $84, $84, $81; right $85, $87, $82. TIME OUT and GAME OVER share their middle sprite ($84)
the middle sprite of each message: $84 for TIME OUT and for GAME OVER, $81 for CONTINUE
the right-hand sprite of each message: $85, $87 and $82

the continue question: left picks YES, right NO, each flashing in turn ($612C, $6166) by inverting part of the CONTINUE sprites; fire takes the answer once the chosen word shows normally, and uses up a continue ($DBEA)
every other call inverts the bytes of YES in the CONTINUE sprites ($E02A-$E07F)
every other call inverts the bytes of NO in the CONTINUE sprites ($E06A-$E0BF)
swaps $6301-$6500 with the sprite shapes at $E000-$E1FF, 512 bytes, and flips the flag $03F5
clears the screen at $CC00 down to its hidden rows, and the colour RAM from $DAE8 to its end
colours the panel's four rows ($DB48-$DBE7) by the character in each cell, through the table that starts at $0768 (so $0800 for character $98)
shows the screen at $CC00 with the characters at $C800, copied from $6501-$6800, black background
writes the 30-character message at $677D and $679B on the loading screen, two rows, in colour 8; used by the game over before the high scores
puts the eight characters of the loading text that change with the level ($03FC) into it, from the tables at $67D9-$6840
writes the 34-character loading text at $6739 and $675B on the loading screen, two rows, in colour 8
writes the loading text before the ending, from $6739/$675B and $67B9/$67C9
the interrupt during loading: a band of 30 lines painted in the border and the background, one colour a line from the table at $6841, timed by delays
points the IRQ vector straight at irq_loading_bars, turns the sprites off and asks for the interrupt at line $6A
a lone RTS, called three times by the loading bars as a delay

eight sprite shapes kept here and swapped into $E000-$E1FF when needed ($6198): the three of CONTINUE with YES and NO ($80-$82), TIME OUT's ends ($83, $85), the middle that TIME OUT and GAME OVER share ($84), and GAME OVER's ends ($86, $87)
the message sprites from $84 on, the second half of the 512 bytes that swap_sprites exchanges with $E100-$E1FF
the loading screen's characters 0 to 70, copied to $C800 with the 3 bytes of texts after them: letters and digits two characters wide and two high, drawn as pairs of codes, one row above the other
the second page of the loading font, copied to $C900
the third page of the loading font, copied to $CA00, which runs on into the loading texts at $6739
the top row of the loading text, 34 codes, eight of them changed with the level ($6237)
the top halves of the world number's big digit in the loading text, filled from level_text_codes
the right-hand top character of the world number's digit
the top halves of the stage number's big digit, filled from level_text_codes
the right-hand top character of the stage number's digit
the bottom row of the loading text, 34 codes
the bottom halves of the world number's big digit
the right-hand bottom character of the world number's digit
the bottom halves of the stage number's big digit
the right-hand bottom character of the stage number's digit
the top row of the message before the high scores ($621D), 30 codes
the bottom row of the message before the high scores, 30 codes
the 16 codes that end the top row of the text before the ending ($6285)
the 16 codes that end the bottom row of the text before the ending

eight tables of 13 codes, indexed by the level 0 to 12: the four characters of the world's big digit (1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5) then the four of the stage's (1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2), put into the loading text at $6755, $6756, $6777, $6778, $6759, $675A, $677B and $677C
the world digit's top right character, by level
the world digit's bottom left character, by level
the world digit's bottom right character, by level
the stage digit's top left character, by level
the stage digit's top right character, by level
the stage digit's bottom left character, by level
the stage digit's bottom right character, by level
the 30 colours of the band behind the loading text, one a line: white, light grey, grey, dark grey, 21 lines of blue, and back to white, then black

the high-score table as the file IH loads it, ten entries of 25 bytes: seven score digits, a name of 16 letters and the level reached as two digits. Manfred Trenz 100,000 at 4-2, Ramiro Vaca, Adam Bulka, Markus W., Alexander Ernst, Chris Huelsbeck and Marc A. Ulrich, then the three lines "!COPYRIGHT 1990!", "!      BY      !" and "! RAINBOW ARTS !" at 30,000, 20,000 and 10,000
six bytes after the high-score table, 0, 0, 0, 0, $FF, $FF, which nothing reads by address

the fast loader: loads the file whose two-letter name is in X and Y from the drive and unpacks it as it arrives. Sends the name ($6B1A), then for each packed chunk takes a five-byte header into $AA-$AE and unpacks it ($698F), until the drive signals the end ($AF bit 6)
operand of the LDY at $6972: load_file keeps Y here while receive_byte runs
operand of the LDX at $6974: the count of the five header bytes still to come, which go to $AE down to $AA

unpacks one chunk, writing downwards from its end address ($AB/$AC): a bit stream ($AA) chooses between runs of bytes taken straight from the drive and copies of bytes already unpacked at a distance it encodes in 2 to 12 bits
reads X bits of the stream into A (and $A5 for more than eight), fetching a new byte from the drive when the bit buffer at $AA runs empty, and counting the packed bytes left ($AD/$AE)
operand of the LDY at $6AB7: 0 when get_bits ran out of bits, 1 when get_bit did, so the refill goes back to the right one
